assessments.rationale: Using a monomaterial polymer maximizes the ease and quality of recycling (parameter d, Page 79) and avoids technical solutions detrimental to recycling (parameter e, Page 79). It prevents the generation of mixed plastic waste that cannot be easily separated, thereby reducing the amounts of waste generated in end-of-life treatment (parameter r, Page 80) and minimizing the environmental footprint of waste treatment (parameter m, Page 33/80). Avoidance of composite polymers also reduces the risk of microplastic and nanoplastic release during mechanical recycling processes (parameter p, Page 80).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with the Manufacturing and Use phases, which may prefer composite polymers for higher mechanical strength, thinner walls (lightweighting), and durability under stress.

assessments.rationale: Reversible mechanical fasteners facilitate the ease of upgrading, reuse, remanufacturing, and refurbishment (parameter c, Page 27/79) by allowing non-destructive disassembly. This choice avoids technical solutions detrimental to reuse, remanufacturing, and recycling (parameter e, Page 79) and ensures high-quality recycling of separated material fractions (parameter d, Page 79), reducing the overall amounts of waste generated (parameter r, Page 80).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with the Manufacturing phase, which prefers permanent chemical adhesives or ultrasonic welding for lower assembly costs, faster cycle times, and reduced part count.

options_evaluated: Modular brushless DC motor with easily removable magnets
Standard brushed AC motor with integrated/glued components
Synchronous reluctance motor with cast rotor
assessments.recommendation: Modular brushless DC motor with easily removable magnets
assessments.rationale: A modular brushless motor allows for easy extraction of high-value components (like rare-earth magnets) and copper windings, which directly improves the ease and quality of recycling (parameter d, Page 79) and material recovery (parameter e, Page 79). This design supports ease of remanufacturing and refurbishment (parameter c, Page 27/79) and prevents valuable materials from being lost to shredding, reducing the environmental footprint of end-of-life treatment (parameter m, Page 33/80).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with the Manufacturing phase due to the higher upfront bill-of-materials cost and complexity of sourcing modular brushless motors.

options_evaluated: Removable/washable open-cell foam filters and heatsinks
Potted electronics and sealed thermal enclosures
assessments.recommendation: Removable/washable open-cell foam filters and heatsinks
assessments.rationale: Potted electronics are highly detrimental to recycling and material recovery (parameter e, Page 79) as they prevent the separation of electronic components from the housing, leading to increased hazardous waste generation (parameter r, Page 80). Removable and washable filters and heatsinks support ease of refurbishment and maintenance (parameter c, Page 27/79) and reduce the energy and resource consumption required during end-of-life processing (parameter g, Page 79).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with the Use and Reliability phases, which may prefer potted electronics to protect sensitive components from dust, moisture, and vibration, thereby extending the product's technical lifetime.

options_evaluated: Highly modular architecture with toolless component swap (separate battery, motor, and cord reel modules)
assessments.recommendation: Highly modular architecture with toolless component swap (separate battery, motor, and cord reel modules)
assessments.rationale: A highly modular architecture directly enhances the ease of upgrading, reuse, remanufacturing, and refurbishment (parameter c, Page 27/79) by allowing individual worn-out modules to be replaced or serviced without discarding the entire product. This avoids solutions detrimental to circularity (parameter e, Page 79), minimizes the amounts of waste generated (parameter r, Page 80), and reduces the energy and resource consumption associated with processing bulk electronic waste (parameter g, Page 79).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with the Manufacturing phase, which may prefer an integrated design to minimize structural parts, reduce weight, and lower production costs.

options_evaluated: Removable and standardized Li-ion battery pack
assessments.rationale: Corded mains power completely avoids the generation of hazardous battery waste (parameter r, Page 80) and eliminates the highly resource- and energy-intensive end-of-life treatment processes required for lithium-ion batteries (parameter g, Page 79). This significantly reduces the environmental and carbon footprint of end-of-life treatment (parameter m, Page 33/80) and avoids technical solutions (like degraded integrated batteries) that are detrimental to the long-term reuse or recycling of the vacuum cleaner (parameter e, Page 79).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with the Use phase, where users demand the portability, convenience, and flexibility of cordless vacuum cleaners.
